key_insight: A compressible Poiseuille-flow channel with two flexible plates can undergo a critical-layer, convective instability in its symmetric wall mode, while the antisymmetric mode is protected by a mid-plane pressure node.
engineering_relevance: This matters for predicting when compliant-wall channels can amplify pressure/flow disturbances, which is relevant to aeroacoustic liners, flow-control devices, and instability mitigation in flexible conduits.
method: Derive coupled dispersion relations for structural-acoustic wall modes in a two-plate channel.
Use a Fredholm solvability argument to obtain closed-form O(M) wavenumber corrections for smooth no-slip shear profiles.
Classify stability with spatial/temporal analysis and Briggs-Bers criteria, comparing results across shear profiles and numerical schemes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement across three independent numerical schemes to one part in 10^9, with the closed-form correction matching numerical differentiation across three shear profiles.
watch_item: The instability appears only above a critical Mach number when an interior critical layer forms, so the result is sensitive to flow compressibility, wall compliance, and the assumed smooth no-slip profile.
paper_title: A critical-layer instability of structural acoustic wall modes in a two-flexible-plate channel with Poiseuille flow: closed-form low-Mach corrections and parity-protected absorption
